pos.personaBrief: Zagallo built a team to 'defend with the ball' (Coaches' Voice), with Trivela noting control beyond mere possession superiority; Brazil kept the ball against man-markers to tire Italy, though it left space behind on transition.

pro.personaBrief: Brazil played out from Piazza and Clodoaldo with short passes but looked for vertical passes to the attacking quartet and Gerson's long switches; after winning the ball Gerson could counter quickly or hold it while the team reorganised.

est.personaBrief: Zagallo's five attackers constantly interchanged positions, Rivellino drifted inside and Tostao worked as pivot and dropped to link, so roles were fluid rather than fixed zones, though the team kept a clear 4-3-3 base and wide full-backs.

lar.personaBrief: Trivela says Brazil was, with Germany, the only side to exploit the flanks: Jairzinho down the right, Carlos Alberto overlapping and crossing, Rivellino on the left as a covering winger, though the best talents (Pele, Tostao, Gerson) played centrally.

blo.personaBrief: Zagallo knew the Mexican heat would stop opponents pressing and set up a low 4-4-1-1 block against structured attacks, with the back four near the box and a compressed pitch; the forwards did not press from the first pass.

mar.personaBrief: No source states Brazil's own marking scheme; it is described as a covering back line with space protection (Clodoaldo screening, Piazza and centre-backs covering), while man-marking is documented only in opponents Uruguay and Italy.

pla.personaBrief: Zagallo said he would not move a centimetre from his general idea (4-3-3), repositioned Piazza to fit his model and kept the same XI, adapting only details such as the possession plan against Italy's man-marking.

res.personaBrief: Brazil 1970 is remembered as the most beautiful football in history, won with attacking play; Zagallo chased goals with attacking subs and did not shut games, and sought to show doubters their worth.

sis.personaBrief: Zagallo relied on supreme talents (Pele, Gerson, Rivellino, Jairzinho) with interchange freedom, but demanded sacrifice and defined duties from all, such as Pele dropping to midfield, Gerson dropping deep and Rivellino covering the left.

jog.personaBrief: The squad combined exceptional technique with exceptional physical preparation for the heat and altitude (Trivela, Lance), with the classic playmaker Gerson at the centre of the team.

bas.personaBrief: A veteran-heavy squad of 1958/62-era players and established stars (Pele, Gerson, Carlos Alberto, Zagallo's own experience) won the title; no emphasis on academy youth.

lid.personaBrief: Zagallo opened by demanding discipline and order, self-sacrifice, while preserving a good atmosphere (Parreira) and rebuilding the confidence of a criticised group, with the union of players emphasised.
